title: 1. Find C-sharp minor
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Recognize C-sharp, D-sharp, F-sharp and G-sharp in the four-sharp key signature.
practiceTip: Start at 40 BPM. Locate the black keys before playing, then practise RH, LH and both. Move on when you can find the notes without searching.

title: 2. Shape the broken chord
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Prepare the opening G-sharp–C-sharp–E shape in slow quarter notes.
practiceTip: Use RH 1–2–4 as a starting fingering. Let the forearm follow the notes; do not hold a rigid stretch. Keep the LH C-sharp quiet. Start at 40 BPM.

title: 3. Three even notes per beat
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Maintain a steady triplet accompaniment without accents.
practiceTip: Count ONE-trip-let, TWO-trip-let, THREE-trip-let, FOUR-trip-let. The three eighth notes share ONE quarter-note beat: at 60 BPM each lasts 1/3 second. Begin at 30–40 BPM.

title: 4. Quiet bass octaves
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Find a relaxed octave and move the whole hand between bass positions.
practiceTip: Practise LH alone at 30–40 BPM. Release before each change and move the forearm; never force the span. Return to single bass notes in step 2 if octaves are not yet comfortable.

title: 5. Let the melody sing
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Hold the upper melody while the inner triplets remain soft and even.
practiceTip: Use finger 5 for the sustained G-sharp and 1–2–3 for the triplets below. Practise RH alone first at 30 BPM. Listen for a singing top note; the app grades pitches, not voicing or how softly you play.

title: 6. Dotted melody against triplets
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Place a dotted eighth and sixteenth over an unchanged triplet pulse.
practiceTip: The short melody note arrives after the third triplet note, not together with it. Clap the melody, then use Listen at 30 BPM and copy it. The last beat divides into 3/4 + 1/4 for the melody but 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 below.

title: 7. Read the chromatic colors
arrangement: Original preparatory exercise; not an excerpt from Beethoven.
description: A focused preparation for Moonlight Sonata, before tackling the original score.
learningFocus: Recognize the raised notes used in the middle of the movement.
practiceTip: The opening RH notes are D-sharp4, E4, E-sharp4 (the F4 key), and F-sharp4. Later, F-double-sharp4 uses G4 and B-sharp3 uses C4. Read the accidental before finding the key; note hints name the physical key. Reset the RH position at each bar and play at your own pace.
